goal.summary: Implement reusable capacity-aware MXFP8 C = A * B^T on the existing Buckyball MXMM Ball. Deliver a callable consumer that executes the frozen request bytes through real RISC-V ELF on focused BEMU.
goal.deliverable: ball/mxmm.py plus all source patches and reproduction assets needed by the frozen CLI contract in acceptance.py.
scope: MXMM host packing, tiling, ISA and focused verification.

Inputs are row-major E4M3 codes and per-row E8M0 scales per 32 K elements; output is FP32. Support M=1 or multiples of 16 up to 64, N positive multiples of 16 up to 80, K positive multiples of 32 up to 4096.
constraints: Use the pinned poly configuration and its actual bank capacities; preserve numerical semantics.
Expose dimensions and input data at the callable interface; do not hardcode case outputs. Repeated calls must not retain stale accumulator state.

Use only the current Task workspace for inspection, edits, builds and outputs. Access the prepared baseline only through the mounted Buckyball checkout tool; do not inspect other preparation or execution roots and do not create sibling/global run directories.

Run: python3 ball/mxmm.py request.json response.json. The request/response schema is the executable contract in acceptance.py; every call carries actual codes/scales and returns C, eight unchanged FP32 guard words and its real command record.

Build and run actual RISC-V ELF on focused BEMU with the MXMM core selected. Record the four existing capacity/window/window-chain/window-rows regression commands and terminal results; BEMU evidence is not RTL correctness.

project.json identifies the pinned baseline and optional BEMU/compiler references. Work in independent prepared checkouts and preserve the baseline for comparison. Never substitute folded, projected or otherwise regenerated inputs for the frozen request bytes.

project.bemu supplies operator-pinned focused BEMU executables. The final checker independently replays each built ELF and regression, reads raw input symbols and compares device output. All ELFs must be built below the fresh consumer directory; command records alone cannot pass. See bemu.py for the device text interface.

criteria.statement: One deterministic fresh-CAS consumer executes ball/mxmm.py on every frozen call, requires successful focused-BEMU command records and the four named regressions, independently derives exact decoded-input products, checks exact FP32 values or the conservative accumulation error bound, verifies repeated calls and output guards, and rejects missing or altered request bytes. Independently replay real RISC-V ELFs using project.bemu, check original input bytes in loadable symbols, device C/guard output and real regression exits.
